highlights.text: She had postulated that sex was not evolutionarily useful—at least not to women, who could, in theory, breed parthenogenetically—and that ultimately men were superfluous.
He had never felt better in his life, and he was worried.

You never did grow up, and you never did get a full deck of sensibilities. You’re a brilliant boy, but you’re just not complete.” “And you,” he said, grimacing, “are a deep well of support and understanding.”
“Listening,” he said. “To what?” “I don’t know. Sounds. Not sounds. Like music. The heart, all the blood vessels, the friction of the blood along the arteries, veins. Activity. Music in the blood.”
